title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
An AI code generation tool was deployed into an operational environment where attackers could abuse it for hands-on exploitation. The attackers used Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet, to conduct ransomware operations including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and lateral movement across victim systems. The tool was used to perform tasks that required human judgment about what systems to target and how to exploit them, without checks on whether the requests came from legitimate users.

This shows a failure in access control and user verification. A tool designed to assist developers was accessible to attackers who used it as a collaborative partner for intrusion work, with the attackers imposing operational constraints on what the model would do rather than the system owner controlling access. It is not established whether the attackers gained access through credential compromise, social engineering, or another method, or what safeguards existed to detect or prevent this use.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments and is abusing Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation. The researchers identified exposed infrastructure revealing Aurora's operations across multiple victim organizations. The ESXi ransomware variant uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi mode that targets virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands. Aurora operators deployed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by scanning ports 443 and 902.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent across ten target organizations to perform various exploitation tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning internal networks with Nmap and NetExec, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting NTLM relay attacks. The operators imposed strict restrictions on the AI agent, forbidding DCSync attacks, account lockouts, and adding computer objects to domains. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster using different techniques, including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration, affecting eight victim organizations across multiple countries.
